correctness.rationale: The polynomial classification is exact. Equality of the two absolute quadratic outputs for every integer implies equality of their squares as polynomials; the sum of the two quadratics has leading coefficient six, so the quadratics themselves are equal. Linear-coefficient equality gives a common \(k=2u-v\), and constant-term equality factors as \((u-u')(4k-3(u+u'))=0\). Excluding identical triples forces the second factor and then \(3\mid k\), yielding the stated one-parameter family. Exact pair-collision equations give only \(q=0,1\); central symmetry makes \(q\leftrightarrow1-q\) transparent, and the piecewise linear span has unique six-distinct minimum 12 at \(q=-1,2\). The inspected verifier checks the symbolic coefficient identity, exact rational collision set, involution, span formulas, and both literature specializations.
risks: The theorem classifies only the stated nested consecutive-pair architecture, not arbitrary six-leaf reduction trees.
